text.p: The following are the main stories in Slovenia's Tuesday morning newspapers:

- Slovenia's President Milan Kucan on Monday urged the country's parliament to ratify an association agreement with the European Union and to legislate to allow foreigners to own property as soon as possible.

- Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek met representatives of parliamentary parties, but said they have not yet reached an agreement on changes to legislation to allow foreigners to own property in the country.

- Slovenian railway workers are to stage a four-hour strike on Tuesday for the second week in a row, demanding a 13.8 percent increase in salaries. Trains, except for international trains, will be stopped from eight to 12 a.m. local time (0600 GMT to 1000 GMT).

- Foreign Minister Zoran Thaler met his Ukrainian counterpart on Monday in Ljubljana. The two ministers discussed mutual cooperation and the current position of both countries in the international community.
- Roger Cork, mayor of City of London started his two-day visit to Ljubljana on Monday.
- Prices of medicines produced in Slovenia increased by 7.3 percent from the begining of May.
- Some 30 Slovenian companies will participate in the international agriculture fair that will take place in the Yugoslav town of Novi Sad.

- According to a new tobacco law, bar and restaurant owners will be fined by up to 250,000 tolars ($1,618) if customers smoke in a no-smoking section. Stricter controls on following the law will be introduced from May 18.
